newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Nedcor yr shr seen robust, FNB up.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Nedcor yr shr seen robust, FNB up.

text.p: Positive growth in interest income and fatter margins in the second half of the year will underpin annual results from two of South Africa's largest commercial banks when they report next week, analysts said.
But First National Bank Holdings Ltd's (FNB) earnings growth was seen hemmed in by a hefty bad debt bill, while Nedcor Ltd was expected to show sturdier growth amid aggressive marketing strategies.
FNB reports results for the year to September 30 on Wednesday followed by Nedcor on Thursday.
"FNB's bad debt charge is going to be up sharply," Doug Ellish, an analyst at Standard Equities said.

Analysts said instalment finance divisions, FirstPref Retail Sales and Wesbank, were largely to blame for the rising debt charge, which one estimated would be up 18 percent on last year's 393.5 million rand.
"FirstPref is the big problem. It was not included (in the financial statements) last year as it was only launched recently," said one analyst.

Analysts polled by Reuters forecast FNB's annual headline earnings up 17 percent to between 243 and 252 cents a share with a consensus of 247.8 cents. They expected a dividend of 77.4 cents compared with 66 cents a year ago.
Whereas FNB was seen having problems with its instalment finance divisions, Nedcor was seen raking in new business in this area after embarking on an aggressive marketing drive.
"They have had good market penetration especially in instalment credit, although this is coming off a low base," Ellish said.

Analysts expect Nedcor's year headline earnings to rise to between 477 and 480 cents with consensus pegged at 478.6 cents -- a 24 percent increase on last year's 386 cents. The dividend was seen climbing to 149 cents from 119 previously.
Tight cost controls and conservative debt provisioning was seen boosting Nedcor's growth with headline earnings expected to breach the one billion rand level for the first time.
Analysts said FNB's advances would grow but at a slower rate than its competitors to whom it was losing market share.
"They seem to have lost the ability to come up with innovative products. When Nedcor launched NedCredit, the other banks responded...FNB did not come up with anything," one said.
Some analysts felt it was difficult to predict earnings for FNB following the appointment of a new managing director after the resignation of Barry Swart amid a nepotism scandle.
"With the putting in place of a new MD they may want to clear their books and start from a lower base," an analyst said.
But others disagreed: "FNB has lost a lot of market share, not only at the corporate, but also at the retail level. I think they will want to push up their earnings."
